definition: A combinational circuit that selects one of several input lines and forwards it to a single output line. Think of it as a digitally controlled switch.
how_it_works: 1. The circuit has 2^n data inputs (D0, D1, D2...), n selection lines (S0, S1...), and 1 output (Y). 2. Based on the binary value of the selection lines, exactly one data input is connected to the output. For example, if selection is 00, Y = D0; if selection is 01, Y = D1.

logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Match the data bus widths to Data Bits and the selector width to Select Bits. With the default east-facing layout and bottom selector, connect data on the west, the selector on the south, and the output on the east. Check Facing and Select Location if the symbol is rotated. If the optional Enable pin is present, drive it high for normal operation.

comparison.key_difference: A MUX routes many inputs to ONE output. A DEMUX routes ONE input to many outputs. They perform opposite routing functions.

troubleshooting: If the output always matches D0, attach a Probe to the selector and verify that it changes from zero. Use different values on the data inputs so the selected input is visible at the output.
If the output is zero or undefined with Enable low, check Disabled Output and drive Enable high.
For a width mismatch, check the selector and data buses separately. A four-input MUX takes a 2-bit selector even when each data input is only 1 bit wide.

definition: A combinational circuit that takes a single input signal and routes it to one of several output lines based on selection inputs. It performs the reverse function of a multiplexer.
how_it_works: With n select bits there are 2^n outputs. The selected output carries the input word. For example, select 10 routes the word to Y2. In Logisim-evolution, the unselected outputs are zero or floating depending on Three-State?. An undefined selector does not identify an output.

logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Set Select Bits to the selector width and Data Bits to the routed word width. Drive the data and selector inputs. Drive the optional Enable high if present. Select codes count from zero. Use Probes to inspect the outputs.

comparison.key_difference: A DEMUX routes ONE input to many outputs. A MUX routes many inputs to ONE output. Use a MUX to choose between signals, use a DEMUX to send one signal to different destinations.

troubleshooting: If an unselected output is floating, check Three-State? before changing the wiring. Attach a Probe to observe the signal.
If the selected output is unexpected, check the selector value and bit order. With 2 select bits, binary 10 selects Y2.
If all outputs are undefined, check that the selector is fully driven and the optional Enable input is high.

definition: A combinational circuit that converts binary information from n input lines to a maximum of 2^n unique output lines. Exactly one output is active (1) at any time based on the input combination.
how_it_works: 1. The circuit has n input lines and 2^n output lines. 2. For each binary input combination, exactly one corresponding output is 1; all others are 0. For example, 2-to-4 decoder: input 01 makes output Y1=1, Y0=Y2=Y3=0. This is essentially a binary-to-one-hot converter.

logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Set Select Bits to the input code width. Drive the select input with a Pin and observe each output with a Probe or LED. If the optional Enable pin is present, drive it high during testing. Check the pin labels and orientation on the selected component.

comparison.key_difference: A Decoder sets the selected output to 1 and others to 0. A DEMUX routes the actual input signal value to the selected output. A Decoder has no data input (only selection); a DEMUX has both data and selection inputs.

troubleshooting: To test a 2-to-4 decoder as a black box, apply 00, 01, 10, and 11 in turn and verify that Y0, Y1, Y2, and Y3 respectively are asserted. Confirm signal values on the actual output pins.
If no output is asserted, check that the select bus is driven and the optional Enable is high. Check the setting that controls whether inactive outputs are zero or floating.
If more than one output seems active, probe the output pins individually and check for accidentally joined nets.

definition: A combinational circuit that adds two single-bit binary numbers. It produces a Sum and a Carry output but cannot accept an input carry from a previous stage.
how_it_works: 1. Two inputs: A and B. Two outputs: Sum (S) and Carry (C_out). 2. Sum = A XOR B. Carry = A AND B. 3. Truth table: 0+0 gives S=0, C=0; 0+1 gives S=1, C=0; 1+0 gives S=1, C=0; 1+1 gives S=0, C=1. The Half Adder is insufficient for multi-bit addition because it lacks a Carry-in input.

required_blocks: Pin (x2, for inputs A and B)
Pin or Probe (x2, for outputs Sum and Carry)
logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Feed A and B into both the XOR and AND gates. XOR produces the low result bit and AND produces the carry. Test all four input combinations. For 1 + 1, the two-bit result is 10, with Carry=1 and Sum=0.

comparison.key_difference: A Half Adder has NO Carry-in input, so it can only add the two least significant bits (LSB) of multi-bit numbers. A Full Adder has a Carry-in input, making it chainable for multi-bit addition.

troubleshooting: If Sum is 1 for A=B=1, check whether the Sum gate is OR instead of XOR. If Carry is also 0, inspect the carry path separately.
If the outputs appear swapped for A=B=1, verify that the XOR goes to Sum and the AND goes to Carry.

definition: A combinational circuit that adds three single-bit binary numbers: two operands (A and B) and a Carry-in (C_in) from the previous bit position. It outputs a Sum and a Carry-out (C_out).
how_it_works: 1. Three inputs: A, B, C_in. Two outputs: Sum, C_out. 2. Sum = A XOR B XOR C_in. C_out = (A AND B) OR (C_in AND (A XOR B)). 3. A Full Adder can be built from two Half Adders and an OR gate: first Half Adder adds A and B, second Half Adder adds its Sum with C_in. The final Carry-out is the OR of the two Half Adders' Carry outputs.

required_blocks: Pin or Probe (x2, for Sum, C_out)
logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Chain: XOR1(A,B) -> Sum_intermediate. XOR2(Sum_intermediate, C_in) -> Final Sum. AND1(A,B) -> Carry1. AND2(Sum_intermediate, C_in) -> Carry2. OR(Carry1, Carry2) -> C_out. To make a multi-bit adder, connect C_out of bit 0 to C_in of bit 1.

comparison.key_difference: Full Adder has a Carry-in (C_in) input, making it chainable for adding multi-bit numbers (like in a Ripple Carry Adder). Half Adder lacks C_in, so it can only add the LSB.

troubleshooting: If A=B=C_in=1 gives anything other than Sum=1 and C_out=1, probe the two XOR stages and both inputs to the carry OR gate. In that case the first XOR is 0, the first carry term is 1, and the second carry term is 0.
When chaining stages, try 0011 + 0001. A result other than 0100 can reveal a missing or reversed carry connection. Carry propagates from the least significant bit toward the most significant bit.

definition: A digital functional unit that selects and performs an arithmetic or logic operation on binary operands. A basic fixed-width ALU uses combinational logic and may expose status flags.
how_it_works: Functional blocks can calculate candidate results in parallel. The operation code selects the result through a MUX. Common flags are Z (all result bits are zero), N (result MSB), C (unsigned carry-out for addition), and V (signed overflow). For fixed-width two's-complement addition, V is set when the input signs match and the result sign differs. For subtraction, V is set when the operand signs differ and the result sign differs from A. Borrow and carry conventions for subtraction depend on the design.

required_blocks: AND, OR, XOR, NOT gates (for logic)
logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Connect operands A and B to the arithmetic and logic blocks. Route results of the same width to a MUX and wire the operation code to its selector. Use the Adder and Subtractor blocks for separate arithmetic paths, or implement subtraction with A + NOT(B) + 1. To produce Z, reduce all selected result bits with OR and invert the result. If an operation has its own flags, select them with the same operation code.

comparison.key_difference: An Adder can only add numbers. An ALU can perform MULTIPLE operations (ADD, SUB, AND, OR, SLT) based on a control signal. The ALU uses a MUX to choose the result.

troubleshooting: If a MUX data input has the wrong width, check each operation's output before connecting it. Use explicit extension where a result is narrower.
Use 4-bit addition examples to separate flags: 0111 + 0001 produces 1000 with signed overflow and no carry-out. 1111 + 0001 produces 0000 with carry-out and no signed overflow.
If the Zero flag follows the bits individually, split the result bus into one-bit signals and reduce them to a single output.

definition: A clocked sequential circuit that captures the value on its D (Data) input at the active edge of the clock signal and holds it stable on the Q output until the next active clock edge. It is a 1-bit memory element and the fundamental building block of registers.
how_it_works: With edge triggering configured, the component samples D at the selected clock edge and holds Q between edges. The usual default is the 0-to-1 edge. Asynchronous Set and Reset can force the stored value without waiting for an edge. When checking sequential behavior from the outside, compare Q before and after an edge and control the starting state.

logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Wire D to the data input and the clock source to the triangle-marked input. Probe Q. Check the Trigger setting and keep asynchronous Set and Reset inactive while testing ordinary sampling. For a manual test, change D first, then create the configured edge on the clock input.

comparison.key_difference: A D Flip-Flop is EDGE-triggered (updates only at clock edge). A D Latch is LEVEL-sensitive (Q follows D transparently while Enable=1). For state machines and registers, always use edge-triggered Flip-Flops to prevent timing hazards.

troubleshooting: If Q is stuck, probe the clock input, verify Trigger, and check that Set or Reset is not forcing the output.
If Q follows D while the clock is held at one level, check whether Trigger is configured for a level instead of an edge.
For intended synchronous state feedback, route Q through the next-state logic to D. Check for a separate unintended path that forms a loop using only combinational elements.

definition: A digital circuit composed of multiple D Flip-Flops sharing a common clock signal, capable of storing a multi-bit binary word. It is the state memory element in Moore and Mealy finite state machines.
how_it_works: A parallel register stores an N-bit word. With edge triggering and writing enabled, the register captures the whole data word on the configured edge. In an FSM, Q represents the current state and D represents the candidate next state. Returning Q through the next-state logic to D closes a feedback path through memory, so the transition depends on stored state.

required_blocks: Clock generator (or manual Button for single steps)
Pin (for Data input, set Data Bits to N)
logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Set Data Bits to the state or data width. Connect the input bus to D, read the stored bus at Q, and wire the clock to the triangle input. Check the configured Trigger. Drive write enable high for updates, and keep asynchronous reset low during normal operation. Pulse reset to establish an all-zero state when the design uses zero as its starting code.

comparison.key_difference: A D Flip-Flop stores 1 bit. A Register stores N bits in parallel. In Logisim, a Register with Data Bits=1 is functionally a D Flip-Flop, but the Register component provides a cleaner interface for multi-bit state storage with built-in enable and clear options.

troubleshooting: If Q stays constant after a clock edge, probe D, the clock and write enable, and check reset.
If the FSM always changes state, examine the transition table. An explicit hold case uses next state equal to current state.

To reproduce an error, reset before each test and record the input sequence, the sampled edges, and Q after each step. The same present input can give different results when the initial state or earlier inputs differ.

definition: A component that produces a periodic oscillating digital signal (alternating between 0 and 1 at a fixed frequency) used to synchronize all sequential elements in a digital circuit. It is the heartbeat of any synchronous design.
how_it_works: The Clock alternates between logic 0 and 1. In Logisim-evolution, High Duration and Low Duration are measured in simulator ticks. One full cycle takes their sum in ticks, so a tick rate of 8 Hz with one tick high and one low gives 4 clock cycles per second.

required_blocks: Clock (from Wiring folder) OR Pin/Button (for manual ticking)
Probes or LEDs (optional, to visualize clock signal)
logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Place Clock from Wiring and connect its output to the clock inputs of the sequential elements. Set High Duration and Low Duration on the component. Use the Simulate menu to enable automatic ticks and choose Tick Frequency. For debugging, advance individual ticks and probe the signal to see when the configured active edge occurs.

comparison.key_difference: The Clock component runs AUTOMATICALLY at a set frequency. A Button/Pin configured as Clock requires manual clicking (via Poke tool) for each tick. Use automatic Clock for fast simulation; use a Button for step-by-step debugging to observe state changes slowly.

troubleshooting: If the clock output stays fixed, check whether automatic ticks are enabled. For manual debugging, verify the signal actually crosses the receiving component's configured edge.
If an FSM seems to advance only every second tick, check the durations and Trigger settings. With one tick high and one low, successive rising edges are two ticks apart.

definition: A finite-state machine whose output function uses only the current state. The inputs can still affect which state is entered next.
how_it_works: Describe the states, initial state, allowed inputs, and transitions. Compute next state from current state and input, then store it on the active clock edge. Assign each state its output. In the turnstile example, start Locked, move to Unlocked after payment, and return to Locked after passage. The unlock signal is 1 exactly while the stored state is Unlocked.

required_blocks: Clock or manually driven clock Pin
Logic gates for next state and output
logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Encode Locked as 0 and Unlocked as 1. Feed the current state and event inputs into the logic derived from the transition table. Wire its output to D. Use Q as the unlock output and feed it back to the transition logic. Decide explicitly what happens when both events arrive together.

comparison.key_difference: Moore output is a function of the state only. Mealy output can depend on both state and present input. Both machines can use present inputs to compute the next state.

troubleshooting: Reset to Locked and apply payment with the clock held steady. Unlock should change only after the active edge stores Unlocked, assuming reset stays inactive.
If Unlock follows the payment input directly, trace the output path to check that the output is derived from Q.

definition: A finite-state machine whose output can depend on both the current state and the current input.
how_it_works: For each state and input, define both the next state and the output. A clocked register stores the state while combinational logic computes the outputs. For a turnstile, an alarm can assert when the current state is Locked and a passage attempt is present, even before the next state is sampled.

required_blocks: Clock or manually driven clock Pin
Logic gates for next state and output
logisim_recipe.wiring_tip: Feed Q and the event inputs into the next-state logic and wire its result back to D. Feed Q and the relevant event inputs separately into output logic. With Locked encoded as 0, the alarm example is NOT(Q) AND Passage. Use a Probe to observe the alarm independently of the state.

comparison.key_difference: A Mealy output may respond to an input change between clock edges. A Moore output is derived from the stored state.

troubleshooting: If Alarm changes between clock edges while Q stays fixed, that is consistent with an unregistered Mealy output.
Test the same Passage input once in Locked and once in Unlocked. If the alarm does not distinguish those states, check the Q connection and the polarity of the state encoding.

definition: The study of control and communication across machines, living organisms, and social systems.
how_it_works: A system obtains information, chooses an action, and can adjust its behavior against a goal. A thermostat measures room temperature and adjusts heating relative to a setpoint. Norbert Wiener's 1948 book helped establish cybernetics as a discipline.

definition: A set of interacting elements considered as a whole within a chosen boundary.
how_it_works: Describe the inputs, outputs, internal state, and external disturbances. In control problems, the plant is the object being controlled and the controller chooses the input. A timer heater operates open-loop, while a thermostat uses measured temperature in a closed loop.

definition: Cybernetic analysis relates a goal, information about the system, an action, and its observed result.
how_it_works: Define the boundary and goal, identify available measurements and actions, then account for channel noise and delays. Feedback organizes control, communication carries signals, and black-box analysis is one option for modeling behavior.

definition: The return of information about a system's state or output to influence subsequent control actions.
how_it_works: A controller can act on the error e(t) = r(t) - y(t), where r is the setpoint and y is the measured output. A thermostat reduces heating as temperature rises. Excess gain or delay can cause oscillation even with negative feedback.

comparison.key_difference: Negative feedback counteracts a deviation. Positive feedback reinforces a change, as when a microphone picks up sound from its own speaker.

definition: Delivery of a message from a source to a receiver through a communication channel.
how_it_works: An encoder represents the source message for transmission and a decoder recovers it at the receiving end. Noise, loss, limited capacity, and delay affect measurements and commands. Coding can detect or correct some errors, and lost data may require a fallback mode.

definition: Shannon entropy measures the average uncertainty of a random variable given its outcome probabilities.
how_it_works: For discrete X, H(X) = -sum_i p_i log2(p_i), with zero-probability terms counted as zero. The unit is bits and a uniform distribution maximizes entropy for a fixed number of outcomes. Mutual information I(X;Y) = H(X) - H(X|Y) gives the average uncertainty reduction about X after observing Y.

definition: The study of control and information processing in engineered systems.
how_it_works: It covers regulation, tracking, sequencing, state estimation, diagnosis, and adaptation. A motor controller uses measured speed to adjust its input as the load changes. A suitable conventional controller can perform this task.

definition: The study and modeling of control, communication, and information processing in living systems.
how_it_works: It models selected processes such as neural signaling and homeostasis. For example, thermoregulation changes heat production and heat loss when body temperature leaves its working range.

definition: The application of systems, information, and control models to economic processes.
how_it_works: A store uses observed sales and stock to choose an order quantity, then updates its decision after delivery and new sales. Demand changes and supply delays act as disturbances. An observed association between price and sales requires further evidence to establish causality.

definition: The study of formal models of information, computation, and control.
how_it_works: Tools include automata, computability and complexity, information theory, optimization, and dynamical models. A turnstile automaton describes locked and unlocked states and their transitions under payment and passage events. A controller also has to compute its action within the required time.

definition: A method of modeling a system from observed inputs and outputs while abstracting from its internal structure.
how_it_works: Apply or observe inputs and record the outputs across relevant operating conditions. A motor's speed response can be estimated from voltage measurements and validated within a tested range. Several internal mechanisms can produce the same external behavior.

comparison.key_difference: Black-box modeling starts from observed behavior. White-box modeling explains behavior using known internal structure and laws.

definition: A model that uses the internal structure and known mechanisms of a system to explain its behavior.
how_it_works: A room model can predict temperature from heater power, heat capacity, and energy losses. A gray-box model combines known structure with parameters estimated from data. In software testing, white-box tests use knowledge of internal code or structure.

definition: An AI model whose individual outputs are difficult to explain in human terms.
how_it_works: Many parameters, nonlinear interactions, and distributed representations can make a trained model hard to interpret. Its weights can remain fixed during inference. Independent validation, error analysis, and checked explanations help assess reliability.

comparison.key_difference: AI opacity concerns interpreting a particular result. The black-box principle concerns studying a system through its input-output behavior.

definition: The field of building systems that perform tasks such as perception, reasoning, planning, learning, and action selection.
how_it_works: Approaches include symbolic rules, machine learning, and search. A learned model can predict equipment load while a controller separately decides how to respond. Generalization depends on data quality and independent evaluation.

definition: An approach to modeling cognition using networks of simple interconnected computational elements.
how_it_works: A concept can be encoded by the activity of many elements. Learning adjusts connection parameters from data, and the elements jointly transform inputs. A network can learn to recognize handwritten digits from examples and be evaluated on unseen digits.

definition: Parameterized models made of connected computational units.
how_it_works: A feedforward network computes a prediction from the input and its parameters. Training adjusts the parameters to reduce a loss, while inference uses the current parameters. Recurrent networks can retain a changing state distinct from their learned weights.

definition: A family of search methods that create variants and select candidates using a quality criterion.
how_it_works: Evaluate a population, select candidates, and produce variants through mutation and sometimes recombination. Controller tuning can rank candidates by error, settling time, and energy use. Many evaluations may be needed, and a global optimum is not guaranteed.

definition: John Searle's 1980 thought experiment about symbol processing and understanding.
how_it_works: A person who does not know Chinese follows written rules to produce convincing Chinese replies. Searle argues that syntax alone does not yield semantics. The systems reply suggests that the whole setup might understand even if the person does not. This is a philosophical dispute about understanding.

definition: The stage of production mechanization driven by water and steam power, beginning around the second half of the eighteenth century.
how_it_works: Mechanized spinning and weaving expanded factory production. Mechanical governors illustrate that feedback control existed in technology before cybernetics became a discipline.

definition: The stage of electrification and mass production associated with the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.
how_it_works: Electric motors gave factories more flexibility in placing machinery. Standardized parts, division of labor, and assembly lines supported repeated operations at scale.

definition: The stage of industrial automation based on electronics, computers, and programmable control, emerging in the second half of the twentieth century.
how_it_works: Programmable logic controllers read sensors and operate actuators, while CNC machines and industrial robots automate production tasks. These controllers can also form part of connected Industry 4.0 systems.

definition: Connected manufacturing that integrates physical equipment, computing, and data to coordinate production.
how_it_works: Sensor readings can feed fault prediction and maintenance scheduling. Cyber-physical systems, industrial IoT, and digital twins can support the integration. Full autonomy and AI in every device are optional.

comparison.key_difference: Industry 3.0 emphasizes programmable automation. Industry 4.0 adds integration across equipment, data, and production processes.

definition: Application of cybernetic principles through measurement, information processing, control action, and observation of the result.
how_it_works: A speed sensor reports a motor's rotation rate, a controller compares it with the setpoint, and a drive adjusts the motor. The next reading shows the effect of the action. Connected manufacturing can link local loops to analytics and scheduling.

definition: Networked physical devices that gather or exchange data and can execute commands.
how_it_works: A sensor or device uses a local network or a gateway to send data to a service or controller. A truck sensor can report cargo temperature. Access control, maintenance, and behavior during connection loss affect reliability.

comparison.key_difference: IoT emphasizes connectivity and data exchange. Cyber-physical systems emphasize the interaction between computation and the physical process.

definition: Systems in which computing and physical processes are tightly coupled.
how_it_works: Sensors report the physical state, a controller computes an action, and actuators change the process. A position controller then measures the new position. Deadlines depend on the process, and reliable measurements and safe failure behavior matter.

definition: A digital representation of a particular physical asset or process that is updated with data about it.
how_it_works: Motor current, vibration, and temperature can update a model used to assess heating under load or test maintenance scenarios. Update frequency and fidelity depend on the task. The model and measurement uncertainty require validation.

comparison.key_difference: A digital twin stays linked to data about a particular asset or process. A standalone simulation can run without that link.

definition: The use of data and models to estimate future or unobserved events.
how_it_works: Define the target, use data available at prediction time, fit on past data, and evaluate on independent observations. For time-dependent tasks, validate on a later period. A model can estimate a motor's failure probability, after which a person or controller chooses an action. Monitor missed events, false alarms, and changes in operating conditions.

definition: An information system that helps people evaluate alternatives using data, models, and criteria.
how_it_works: A maintenance planner can compare immediate repair, weekend repair, and continued operation using failure risk, downtime cost, and staff availability. Conflicting criteria and uncertain data can leave several defensible choices.

comparison.key_difference: Predictive analytics estimates what may happen. Decision support uses predictions and other evidence to compare possible actions.
